mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 8.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% during a recession signals aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS < 1.0% and UNRATE > 7.0% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment losses (PAYEMS < 0) for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market crisis, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and S&P 500 forward returns: higher monthly PAYEMS growth is associated with higher 5-day forward returns, reflecting improved consumer purchasing power and earnings expectations.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between monthly PAYEMS growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.
